# Release 0 contract fixture corpus

`bin/*.bin` contains committed raw binary fixture bundles. Each bundle uses a test-only 40-byte `R0FXBIN\0` envelope followed by exact raw Boot Entry, handoff, memory-map, and RHD byte sequences. The envelope carries only fixture lengths, expected result, and the observed snapshot generation supplied to the host oracle; it is not a RAR OS public contract.

`generate.sh` deterministically recreates every binary from `cases.v1`. `run.sh` compares regenerated bytes with the committed corpus. In the pinned Linux CI route, `reference.rs` is compiled as unsafe-free host-only code and validates the raw bytes with checked unsigned arithmetic. It never dereferences fixture addresses or performs device access.

The binary corpus covers valid x86-64/APIC/16550-I/O and AArch64/GICv3/PL011 values plus malformed entry framing, alignment, overlap, snapshot generation, critical records, identity, references, memory maps, controller-relative interrupts, typed register windows, address spaces, authority binding, map/RHD consistency, and architecture agreement.

`validation-precedence.v1` is the non-executable predicate corpus. It contains one focused expectation for every one of the 33 canonical predicates and a dual-fault expectation for every one of the 32 adjacent precedence edges. The CI reference oracle derives its expected names and codes from `handoff-v1.fields`, proves exact coverage, and rejects drift. Instrumented target-decoder access-budget evidence remains an R0-003/R0-004 obligation because no target decoder exists in R0-002.
